45a781a3-0127-4272-80ad-71d3b6b971c9.description: What if depression is sometimes linked to your body’s internal sense of time? That’s what researchers from the University of Sydney’s Brain and Mind Centre wanted to know. In a new study, they surveyed patients with depression whose symptoms may reflect problems with their circadian rhythms – like their sleep schedule, how tired they feel in the morning and whether they’re a night owl. And while there’s still a lot of research to be done, this could open up new pathways for mental health treatment. NPR health correspondent Will Stone walks us through the study and its implications. ec511269-9bc7-496b-a940-f7131a3cf1b4.description: Every year, millions of people in the United States develop PTSD from a traumatic event—like a car crash, an assault or freak accident. The work – published in the journal Nature Communications – could help an often-overloaded emergency department team prevent mental health disorders before they start.
